problem: Saying that using divisor n gives "wrong df" is not accurate: the degrees of freedom come from the sample sizes, so they are n1 − 1 and n2 − 1 whatever divisor is used. The real error is that the ratio s1²/s2² built with divisor n is a scaled version of the F statistic and no longer follows F(n1 − 1, n2 − 1), so the table comparison is wrong.
fix: Sample variances use divisor n − 1. With divisor n the ratio is scaled by (n1 − 1)n2 / ((n2 − 1)n1), so it no longer follows the F distribution with df (n1 − 1, n2 − 1) and the critical-value comparison fails.

where: Section 2, procedure bullet for H1: σ1² < σ2²
problem: The bullet says to swap the labels or use F = s2²/s1², but it does not say that the df pair and hence the table entry must also be swapped. A student who only flips the ratio will read the critical value with df in the wrong order, which the same chapter warns about elsewhere.
fix: For H1: σ1² < σ2², swap the samples so that the variance expected to be larger is on top: F = s2²/s1² with df1 = n2 − 1 and df2 = n1 − 1, and compare with F(α, n2 − 1, n1 − 1).

problem: The example jumps to the F test without stating the normality assumption that the test needs; the two samples are only described by n and s, and a reader cannot tell whether the test is legitimate here.
fix: Add one line: assume the fill volumes from each machine are independent and approximately normal, so the F-test applies.
